title: "About"

## Welcome to Statistical Hooks

This site is a collection of statistical **hooks** - quick, memorable ways to open a topic, grab attention, and make an abstract concept feel concrete before you dive into the technical details. The idea is simple: 

- if you can hook students' curiosity early, you can hold their attention longer once the harder explanations start.
- They also work well as a reset: a way to re-energise the room after wrapping up a dense topic, before moving on to the next.

The resource is currently split into two main sections, with a third on the way.

**Demonstration Hooks** are designed for larger classes, like lectures, where the instructor leads the activity (think a card trick, a rigged coin flip, or a jar of lollies passed around the room). These work well as a live, front-of-room demonstration: you're doing the trick, and the class is watching, guessing, and reacting together. They're a great way to open a lecture or transition between topics without needing every student to have a device in hand.

**Interactive Hooks** flip the above dynamic. Students engage directly with an app or activity themselves, often game-like in nature. These can still work in a lecture setting, but I've mostly used them in smaller classes, like tutorials, where everyone can get hands-on. Many include a built-in scoring system, and students genuinely respond to that competitive edge — it's a small addition that adds a surprising amount of engagement.

A third section, **Stories**, is coming soon — a collection of interesting real-world stories you can bring into class to illustrate statistical ideas in action.

Below is quick summary table of the hooks and the area (topic) where they could be used:

```{r, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}

library(gt)
library(dplyr)
library(stringr)
library(purrr)

tbl <- data.frame(
  Type = c(
    rep("Demonstration", 14),
    rep("Interactive", 12)
  ),
  
  Hook = c(
    "Jar of Lollies",
    "Bad Graphs Gallery",
    "Class Polls",
    "Lady Tasting Tea",
    "Four Aces",
    "Loaded Dices",
    "Stacked Deck",
    "Heads every time",
    "Psychopath Test",
    "Heart Rates",
    "Contagious Yawns",
    "Skittle Science",
    "Movie Posters",
    "Find your cluster",
    
    "The Witness Test",
    "Monty Hall",
    "Rock Paper Scissors",
    "10 Second Challenge",
    "Surveyor Builder",
    "Stack Game",
    "Color Game",
    "World Cup Simulator",
    "The Stolen Laptop",
    "Should We Launch It?",
    "The Life Ledger",
    "Box Office Model Builder"
  ),
  
  Topics = c(
    "Descriptive Statistics, Sampling, Estimation, Wisdom-of-Crowds",
    "Data Visualisation, Misleading Graphs, Critical Thinking",
    "Confidence Intervals, Sampling, Proportions, Live Data",
    "Hypothesis Testing, Combinatorics, Experimental Design, p-values",
    "Probability, Sampling, Conditional Probability, Multiplication Rule",
    "Central Limit Theorem, Simulation, Discrete Probability, Sampling Distributions",
    "Hypothesis Testing, Null Hypothesis, Type I Error, Probability",
    "Binomial Distribution, Probability, Expected Value",
    "Between-subjects, Independent samples t-test, Group comparisons",
    "Within-subjects, Paired t-test, Repeated Measures ANOVA",
    "Correlation, Linear Regression, Data Collection",
    "Chi Square Test, Goodness of Fit, Categorical Data, Expected vs Observed",
    "Inter-rater reliability, Cohen's Kappa, Agreement, Categorical Data",
    "K-means clustering, Unsupervised learning, Multivariate Data, Standardisation",
    
    "Eyewitness memory, Uncertainty",
    "Probability, Conditional Probability, Simulation, Bayesian",
    "Sampling, Law of large numbers, Randomness, Sampling",
    "Residuals, Normal Distribution, Measurement Error",
    "Estimation, Sampling Bias, Survey Design, Standard Error",
    "Hypothesis Testing, Between-subjects, Independent samples t-test",
    "Permutation Tests, Bootstrap, Between-subjects, Resampling",
    "Likelihood, Simulation, Monte Carlo, Probability Models",
    "Bayesian, Prior & Posterior, Sequential Updating",
    "Bayesian, Prior & Posterior, Beta-binomial Distribution, Sequential Updating",
    "Survival Analysis, Hazard Function, Competing Risks",
    "Multiple Regression, Variable Selection, Model Fit"
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Build a consistent topic -> colour lookup
all_topics <- tbl$Topics |>
  str_split(",\\s*") |>
  unlist() |>
  str_trim() |>
  unique() |>
  sort()

palette <- c(
  "#2E5C8A", "#B8862E", "#1E5B33", "#B3423A",
  "#6B4C9A", "#1F8A8A", "#8A4B2E", "#4B6B8A",
  "#2E7D6B", "#8A2E5C"
)

topic_colors <- setNames(
  rep(palette, length.out = length(all_topics)),
  all_topics
)

make_badges <- function(topics_str) {
  topics <- str_trim(str_split(as.character(topics_str), ",\\s*")[[1]])
  
  badges <- map_chr(topics, function(t) {
    col <- unname(topic_colors[t])
    if (is.na(col) || length(col) == 0 || col == "") {
      col <- "#666666"
    }
    
    paste0(
      "<span style='background:", col, 
      "; color:white; padding:3px 10px; border-radius:999px; ",
      "font-size:11px; font-weight:600; margin:2px; display:inline-block;'>",
      t,
      "</span>"
    )
  })
  
  paste(badges, collapse = " ")
}

gt(tbl) |>
  text_transform(
    locations = cells_body(columns = Topics),
    fn = function(x) map(x, ~ html(make_badges(.x)))
  ) |>
  cols_label(Topics = "Topics") |>
  cols_width(Topics ~ px(400))
```
